sections.title: A Spring Boot app on AWS

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: This is the reference shape to draw from memory, and then adapt to your project.

blocks.title: Reference architecture
blocks.code:
flowchart TD U[Users] --> CF[CloudFront CDN] CF --> S3[S3: React build] CF --> ALB[Application Load Balancer
public subnets, two AZs] ALB --> ECS[ECS Fargate tasks: Spring Boot
private subnets] ECS --> RDS[(RDS PostgreSQL

blocks.caption: Only the load balancer and CDN face the internet; everything else stays private.

components.name: CloudFront and S3
components.description: Serve the React build cheaply and globally, and route `/api` to the load balancer.

components.name: ALB
components.description: Terminates TLS, health-checks tasks and spreads traffic across AZs.

components.name: ECS Fargate
components.description: Runs your container in private subnets, scaled on CPU or request count.

components.name: RDS Multi-AZ
components.description: A synchronous standby for failover. Add read replicas for read scale; they are different things.

components.name: SQS and workers
components.description: Move slow work out of the request, with a dead-letter queue for failures.

rows: Public subnet
Has a route to an internet gateway: load balancers
Private subnet
No inbound internet: applications and databases
NAT gateway
Lets private resources call out; costs per hour and per GB
VPC endpoint
Private path to services such as S3, avoiding NAT
Security group
Stateful firewall per resource: database allows only the app's group
Infrastructure
Terraform or AWS CDK, in Git: no console clicking
Pipeline
GitHub Actions with an OIDC role, no stored AWS keys; push to ECR, then update the service
Release
Rolling, or blue-green; schema changes stay backward compatible
Scaling
Target tracking on ECS; connection pool sizes must fit the database's limit
Backups
Automated RDS snapshots, and test the restore

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: Autoscaling can exhaust database connections: tasks times pool size must stay under the limit. RDS Proxy can help.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **Design this for 99.9% availability on AWS.** Stateless tasks across at least two AZs behind an ALB, RDS Multi-AZ, health checks, autoscaling, backups with tested restores, alarms on user-facing symptoms, and safe deployments. Then state the costs and what you left out, such as multi-region.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Public: load balancer and CDN only.
- Multi-AZ gives availability; read replicas give read scale.
- Infrastructure as code, and OIDC instead of stored keys.
- Check autoscaling against database connection limits.

items.question: What is the difference between RDS Multi-AZ and a read replica?
items.answer: Multi-AZ is a synchronous standby for failover, not used for reads in the classic setup. A read replica is asynchronous and serves reads, so it can lag.

items.question: A task in a private subnet cannot reach an external API. What do you check?
items.answer: The route to a NAT gateway, the security group's outbound rules, and DNS. Check the network ACL too.
